title: rdy/v1 readiness spec
description:
A vendor's readiness requirements (`apiVersion: rdy/v1`, `kind: Readiness`).

Check ids this schema does not know are allowed and reported as not run. Every other unknown key is an error, so a newer spec fails loudly on an older rdy.

apiVersion.description: Format version. Must be `rdy/v1`. Kept as text so the message for a wrong version can quote what the file said.

kind.description: Document kind. Only `Readiness` exists in v1.

metadata.description: Who the spec is for and how fresh it is.

checks.description: The checks to run, in report order. Entries are keyed by id plus optional name, and keys must be unique. A valid spec has 1 to 256 entries.

bundle.description: What `rdy bundle` collects. It parses today so specs written now keep working, and `rdy run` never collects anything.

AbsPath.description: An absolute path: /... on Unix, C:\... on Windows. No control characters.

BundleSpec.description:
The `bundle` block: what `rdy bundle` collects and how it redacts.

It parses in v1 and nothing acts on it yet. `rdy run` never collects anything, whatever this says. Unknown keys are refused.

collect.description: Collectors: `journal:<duration>`, `k8s:events`, `file:<absolute path or glob>`. At most 64.

redact.description: Redactor groups to add, such as `aws_keys`, `bearer_tokens` or `emails`. At most 64. The built-in rules always run, so a spec can add redaction and can never remove it.

redact_patterns.description: Your own patterns, at most 32. A match is replaced with a `custom.<name>` placeholder. A pattern can only add redaction: where it overlaps a built-in match, the whole overlapping region is redacted. A pattern that matches the empty string is an error.

max_size.description: Bundle size cap, such as `200Mi`. It lowers rdy's own cap and never raises it.

Check.description: One check to run: an id, the common fields below, and the parameters of that check id. Parameters of ids this schema does not know are not checked here.

id.description: Which check to run: family.name in lowercase, for example host.memory.

name.description: Short label, shown next to the id. Needed when the same id appears twice.

severity.description: block (the default) makes a failure NOT READY. warn makes it READY with warnings.

fix.description: What the customer should do when this check fails. Plain text. Shown instead of rdy's own advice, which stays available below it.

timeout.description: How long this check may run, 1s to 60s. Replaces the check's own default. Outside that range the check is not run and lint reports an error.

os.description: Run only on these operating systems. On others the check is reported as not applicable and does not count.

allOf.description: Check ids this schema does not know. Their parameters are not checked here; rdy reports the check as not run.

Cidr.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address range such as 10.0.0.0/8 or fd00::/8.

DnsName.description: A host name by the grammar of Target: dot-separated labels of 1 to 63 letters, digits and hyphens that do not start or end with a hyphen. The last label is not a number (2852039166, 0xa9).

Duration.description: A whole number and one unit: ms, s, m, h or d. Examples: 500ms, 10s, 7d.

min.description: Fewer cores than this: the check fails. Container limits count.

recommended.description: Fewer cores than this: the check warns.

arch.description: The host must have one of these architectures. `amd64` is `x86_64` and `arm64` is `aarch64`.

flags.description: CPU flags the host must have, such as `avx2` or `x86-64-v3`. At most 64.

path.description: The install path. When it does not exist yet, the nearest existing parent is measured.

min.description: Less free space than this: the check fails.

recommended.description: Less free space than this: the check warns. The default, `min` plus 20%, is the check's.

min_inodes.description: Fewer free inodes than this: the check fails.

forbid_options.description: Mount options that make the check fail.

forbid_fstypes.description: Filesystem types that make the check fail, such as `nfs`. At most 32.

allow.description: The modes that are fine. Any other mode makes the check fail. Without it every mode is fine.

denials_max.description: More recent denials than this: the check warns. It fails when the context is in `watch`.

denials_window.description: How far back denials count, such as `24h`.

watch.description: Security contexts or programs whose denials make the check fail.

allow.description: The states that are fine. Any other state makes the check fail.

min.description: Less total RAM than this: the check fails, after the tolerance.

min_available.description: Less available RAM than this: the check warns. The default, half of `min`, is the check's.

swap.description: What to do when swap is on. The default is `any`.

tolerance_percent.description: How far below `min` the total may be and still pass, in percent. A 32 GiB machine shows a little less. The default is 5. The check applies it with a floor of 256 MiB. 0 turns it off.

tolerance_result.description: What a total inside the tolerance counts as. The default is `pass`.

supported.description: The distributions the product supports. At most 64.

id.description: The distribution id from `/etc/os-release`, such as `rhel`.

versions.description: The versions that are supported. `"8"` matches a major version and `"22.04"` an exact one. Without it every version is.

arch.description: The host must have one of these architectures.

fips.description: What to expect of FIPS mode. The default is `any`.

windows_min_build.description: The lowest Windows build number that is supported.

free.description: TCP ports that must be free. At most 256.

bind.description: How the product binds it. `public` is the default and means every address. `loopback` means loopback only.

udp_free.description: UDP ports that must be free. At most 256, none twice.

allow_owner.description: Process names that may already hold a port, such as an earlier install of the product.

forbid.description: Agent ids that make the check fail when detected. `rdy spec lint` lists the known ids.

allow.description: Agent ids that are fine when detected.

context_pattern.description: The current kube context must match this pattern, a guard against the wrong cluster.

max_latency.description: A reply slower than this: the check warns. The default, 2s, is the check's.

server_pattern.description: The API server URL must match this pattern.

K8sAdmissionParams.description: Dry-run checks are not supported yet.

pod_security.description: The Pod Security level the product's pods need.

namespace.description: The namespace the product installs into.

scc.description: The OpenShift security context constraint the product documents.

uses.description: Pod features the product needs. The check derives the lowest level from them.

K8sLabelKey.description: A Kubernetes label or taint key: a name, or prefix/name with a lowercase DNS-style prefix.

K8sLabelValue.description: A Kubernetes label or taint value: empty, or up to 63 letters, digits, -, _ and ., starting and ending with a letter or digit.

min_ready.description: Fewer ready nodes than this: the check fails.

min_zones.description: Fewer zones than this: the check fails. Without zone labels it is not evaluated.

per_node.description: Each counted node must have at least this much allocatable. These are allocatable amounts, not the size of the instance.

free.description: The counted nodes together must have at least this much left after the pods' requests.

arch.description: The architectures the counted nodes may have, 1 to 4. `amd64` is `x86_64`.

selector.description: Only nodes with these labels are counted.

tolerations.description: Tolerations that make tainted nodes count, at most 16.

items.description: Without a key the operator must be Exists. With Exists there is no value.

key.description: The taint key. Without it the operator is `Exists` and every taint matches.

operator.description: How the value is compared. Kubernetes treats a missing operator as `Equal`.

effect.description: The effect to tolerate. Without it every effect matches.

can.description: The permissions to test, 1 to 100. Each one is an entry in the audit log of the cluster.

oneOf.description: verb resource[.group][/subresource], as in kubectl auth can-i.

verb.description: The verb. An RBAC verb such as `create`. `*` means all verbs.

group.description: The API group. Empty, which is the default, is the core group.

resource.description: The resource. An RBAC resource such as `namespaces`. `*` means all resources.

namespace.description: The namespace of the object. For a string item this is the `namespace` of the entry.

name.description: The name of the object. Leave it out to mean all names.

namespace.description: The namespace for the string items. The default is cluster scope.

cpu.description: Cores as a number from 0.001 to 1000000 with at most three decimals, or a string of whole cores ("4") or millicores ("500m"), up to 1000000 cores.

class.description: A class that must exist. The default is the cluster's default class.

access_modes.description: Access modes the class must serve, 1 to 4.

binding.description: The binding mode the class must have. The default is `any`.

reclaim_policy.description: The reclaim policy the class should have. A mismatch warns.

max.description: A newer server warns, or blocks with `over_max: block`.

apis.description: APIs the server must serve, 1 to 64. Each one is written `group/version Kind`, or `version Kind` for the core group.

openshift_min.description: The lowest OpenShift version, used when the cluster is OpenShift.

over_max.description: What a server newer than `max` counts as. The default is `warn`.

oneOf.description: A readiness spec. The only kind in `rdy/v1`.

Metadata.description:
The `metadata` block: who the spec is for, which revision it is and when it stops being valid.

Unknown keys are refused.

product.description: Product name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Ties the signature to a trusted key and names the report directory and files.

version.description: Product versions this spec is for, such as `>=4.2`, at most 64 characters. Shown in the report and never evaluated, because rdy cannot know the product version.

contact.description: Where the customer asks questions, at most 256 characters. Shown as plain text, never as a link.

serial.description: Spec revision number, 0 to 9007199254740991. Should go up by at least one on every signed release of this spec. Shown as "Spec revision 7".

expires.description: The UTC time after which rdy refuses to run this spec, in the full form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, for example `2027-01-31T00:00:00Z`. Kept as text here. The shape and the comparison with the clock are checked when the spec is validated.

annotations.description: Up to 32 free-form labels for vendor tooling and the portal. rdy never changes behaviour because of them and copies them into the result. Keys are lowercase, 1 to 63 characters, and values are at most 256 characters.

names.description: The names to look up, 1 to 64.

expect_in.description: Every answer must be inside one of these ranges, 1 to 16.

expect_public.description: The answers must be public addresses (`true`) or private ones (`false`).

max_latency.description: A lookup slower than this: the check warns. The default, 500ms, is the check's.

optional.description: Unreachable gives a warning and not a block. The default is false.

expect_status.description: The statuses that count as reachable, for a URL target. At most 16.

method.description: The request method, for a URL target. The default is `HEAD`.

via_proxy.description: Overrides the `via_proxy` of the entry for this endpoint.

tls.description: `false` probes plain TCP only. Without it TLS is tried for port 443 and `https` URLs.

via_proxy.description: Which path to try. The default is `auto`. `auto` tries what the product would do, and says if the other path works. `direct` uses no proxy. `proxy_only` goes only through the proxy.

trust.description: Which certificates to trust. The default is `system`. `system` is the operating system's store, with the bundled public roots as a fallback. `bundled` is the bundled public roots only.

max_latency.description: A connect slower than this: the check warns. The default, 2s, is the check's.

required_no_proxy.description: Entries that `NO_PROXY` must cover, such as `.svc` or `10.0.0.0/8`.

daemons_need_proxy.description: The container runtime and kubelet must have the proxy too. The default is false.

hosts.description: The hosts to test, 1 to 64. The default is every `net.egress` host in the spec.

expected_issuer.description: A pattern the issuer of the chain must match. A chain from another issuer blocks.

pin_sha256.description: SHA-256 digests of certificates, 1 to 16, each 64 lowercase hex digits.

forbid_interception.description: A chain that only this machine trusts blocks instead of warning. The default is false.

OsFamily.description: An operating system family a check can be limited to.

Quantity.description: Bytes. A whole number with an optional binary suffix Ki, Mi, Gi, Ti, Pi. Decimal suffixes (G, GB) are rejected to avoid ambiguity.

RedactPattern.description: A vendor redaction pattern in the `bundle` block.

name.description: The rule name. A match is replaced with a `custom.<name>` placeholder.

regex.description: The pattern, in Rust `regex` syntax (linear time, no backreferences), 1 to 256 characters. Not compiled here.

Regex.description: A regular expression in Rust regex syntax (linear time, no backreferences).

Severity.description:
How bad a failed check is.

`block` means required: a failure makes the run NOT READY. `warn` means optional: a failure gives READY with warnings. The default is `block`.

oneOf.description: Required. A failure makes the run NOT READY. This is the default.
Optional. A failure gives READY with warnings.

Target.description: host:port, [ipv6]:port, or an http or https URL. Never user:password in a URL; specs carry no credentials.

Version.description: A dotted version such as 1.28 or 5.10, as a quoted string. A bare integer (14) is accepted. An unquoted decimal (1.30) is rejected because YAML reads it as the number 1.3.
